image_description: A side-profile view of a large bison standing in a grassy field. The animal features a massive, shaggy dark brown forequarter with a prominent shoulder hump, transitioning to lighter brown, less furred hindquarters. It has a large head with a visible curved horn, a beard, and sturdy legs partially obscured by tall grass.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large broad head with short curved horns.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible, appearing large and broad relative to the body. One horn is distinctly visible, showing the characteristic short, curved shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beard of long hair on chin and throat.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct mass of long, dark hair hangs from the chin and throat area, matching the description of a bison beard.
The eye is visible as a dark spot on the side of the head, consistent with the expected appearance.
No large, protruding ears are visible; the ear region is covered by the thick mane/fur, which is consistent with the 'hidden' description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Massive body with exceptionally tall, heavily built proportions at the withers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The animal exhibits a massive, heavy build with significant height at the shoulders (withers), tapering towards the rear.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Shaggy dark brown fur covering forequarters forming prominent shoulder hump.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The forequarters are covered in thick, shaggy dark fur that creates a very distinct and prominent hump at the shoulders.
There is a clear visual transition where the fur on the rear half of the body is shorter, smoother, and lighter in color compared to the front.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Short horns compared to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible horn is relatively small and short in proportion to the massive size of the head and body.
The lower portions of the legs and the feet are completely occluded by the tall green grass in the foreground, making it impossible to verify the presence of cloven hooves.
The rear of the bison is cut off by the right edge of the image frame, so the tail is not visible.
